body:
# Verdict: APPROVED

- PASS AC-1: readDetail retries once; the mixed test keeps the board live (4 detail calls) and the persistent-failure test fails closed (6 calls).
- PASS AC-2: A non-default FACTORY_URL is shell-quoted and prefixed; the default is omitted; tests cover default, spaced, and credentialed forms.
- PASS AC-3: The child env is an allowlist plus config env; the sentinel test passes, and stdin/stdout/stderr handlers reject pending calls and replace the child.
- PASS AC-4: One lifetime loop owns the timer with inFlight/queued; route changes only wake it; QA asserts one in-flight board read and both 5-second refreshes.
- PASS AC-5: storage is removed from the board snapshot and derivation, with a focused absence test; the header and cards still render.
- PASS AC-6: A missing script names the resolved path, FACTORY_BOTS_MCP_CONFIG, and a reload hint; the service surfaces it through FailureView.
- PASS AC-7: Typecheck and 60 tests pass, dist matches HEAD, bb plugin list shows factory-bots running, and the screenshots plus QA assertions are committed.

## Security / correctness

No critical or high security/correctness defect. The MCP child runs with shell false, an allowlisted environment, and only read tools. Residual edges are non-blocking: the start command for a relative script omits the config cwd (F-1), a failed transcript refetch keeps the old cache entry (F-2), redaction falls back to the raw string on an unparseable URL (F-4), and script validation treats any path-like argument as a script (F-6).

## Design / maintainability

The split and single-loop wake design are sound. Non-blocking: refs are assigned during render (F-3), the browser QA does not prove an immediate ticket wake and mocks both RPCs (F-5), the shipped factory path is host-specific (F-7), and read-only enforcement lives in the service rather than the client (F-8).

findings.summary: The start command for a relative script omits the config cwd, so it only works from that directory.
A failed transcript refetch leaves the old cache entry, which can be reused for the same stage/conversation.
Refs are assigned during render; a discarded concurrent render could point the loop at an uncommitted selection.
redactUrl returns the raw string when URL parsing fails, so malformed userinfo can be displayed.
The browser QA does not prove an immediate ticket wake and mocks both RPC responses.
Script validation treats every path-like argument as a required script file.
The shipped factory path is developer-specific; a fresh install gets the missing-script error until configured.
callTool accepts any tool name; read-only enforcement lives in the service.
